Maya (runtime): Heads-up — saw a perf regression on /v1/chat in prod after last runtime change. p99 up ~28% on small-seq workloads. nsys traces point to higher global memory traffic + KV cache miss storms when Flash-window-fuse is selected for mixed-length batches.
Samir P: Yep, reproduced locally. tokens/s down ~18% for batch=8, seq=128. Shared mem stalls spike. Looks like fusing across page boundaries is creating heavier smem usage and bank conflicts.
Jonathan R: Can you paste the capture command and a quick repro? I'll run an occupancy sweep.
Maya (runtime): repro steps — run our microbench with pinned seed, warm KV cache 10 iters, then cold start 1 iter. nsys capture used:
```
nsys profile -o /tmp/trace --trace=cuda,osrt --sample=none 
  python perf/bench/flash_compare.py --model gpt-6b --batch 8 --seq 128 --iters 20
```
Samir P: Raw numbers from my run (median of 5):
- flash-window-fuse: p50=11.2ms p95=26.8ms p99=36.5ms
- paged-attn (no fuse): p50=9.9ms p95=19.6ms p99=21.4ms
Memory bw util (sustained): fuse=82% vs paged=58%. KV cache miss rate (per-token): fuse=1.7% vs paged=0.4%.
perf-bot: Profiling snippet (nsys summary):
```
GPU memcpy HtoD: 12.3%
L2 read/write: 36.1%
SM CPI stalled: 28.7% (shared mem contention hotspots)
```
Tess L: Interesting — batching heuristic might be amplifying this. If adaptive-prefix merges short and long sequences, fuse tries to optimize compute but increases smem working set and thrashes KV pages. Try forcing fixed-batch for chat route:
```json
{"batching": {"strategy": "fixed", "max_batch": 8}}
```
Maya (runtime): Agreed. Short-term mitigation: pin kernel selection to `paged-attn` for routes where avg_seq > 64 and variance > 40, and disable fuse across page boundaries. Long-term: we need smarter heuristics that account for KV cache pressure + smem usage.
Jonathan R: I'll run an occupancy sweep today across tile sizes [32,64,128] and pipeline stages [2,3,4] for flash-v2, paged-attn, fused-window. Expected outputs: smem per-thread, occupancy %, bank-conflict counts. I'll dump results to /internal/perf/results/180501.
Samir P: Implementation detail: when fuse merges queries spanning multiple KV pages, we increase per-warp shared mem footprint. That pushes occupancy down (from ~66% to ~45%) which explains the latency tail.
infra-bot: rollout 2026-03-16/runtime-kernel-fuse started on prod canary (3 hosts) — if p99 regresses >15% for 5m, auto-rollback will trigger.
Tess L: Actionable plan:
1) Jonathan: run occupancy sweep + produce csv (owner: @Jonathan R)
2) Samir: prototype fuse gating by KV-warmth heuristic (owner: @Samir P)
3) Maya: flip canary to pinned `paged-attn` if canary shows regression (owner: @Maya (runtime))
4) Perf team: add a KV-warmth signal to console metrics (owner: perf infra)
Jonathan R: I'll also try a quick kernel that uses double-buffered shared mem pipeline (2-stage) — might reduce stalls without sacrificing fusing benefits.
Samir P: If anyone needs quick repro, use: `python perf/bench/flash_compare.py --batch 8 --seqs 64,128,256 --kv-warm 10 --mode cold-first`
Maya (runtime): Great. Please drop results here. If we see consistent p99 improvement with `paged-attn` pinned, we'll patch the selection rule and ship a canary. :thumbsup:
Samir P: :thumbsup:
Jonathan R: Will post CSV and nsys links by EOD.
